studies.Population: Alpha-Tocopherol Beta-Carotene Cancer Prevention Study cohort
studies.Smoking Status: smokers who smoked at least 5 cigarettes/day
studies.Ethnicity Basis: NA: no field-specific ethnicity evidence was available
studies.Reference: Fish, vitamin D, and flavonoids in relation to renal cell cancer among smokers.
studies.Authors: Wilson RT, Wang J, Chinchilli V, Richie JP, Virtamo J, Moore LE, Albanes D
studies.Timing: dietary intake recorded at enrollment; mean follow-up 15.2 person-years from 1985 to 2002
studies.comparison_type: quartile 4 vs. quartile 1 of dietary intake

sample_size.excerpt: Risk was prospectively assessed in the Alpha-Tocopherol Beta-Carotene Cancer Prevention Study (1985-2002) cohort (N = 27,111; 15.2 mean person-years of follow-up).

effect_size.excerpt: Among 228 cases, risk (quartile 4 vs. quartile 1) was associated with consumption of the flavonoid quercetin (hazard ratio = 0.6, 95% confidence interval: 0.4, 0.9; P(trend) = 0.015) and Baltic herring (hazard ratio = 2.0, 95% confidence interval: 1.4, 3.0; P(trend) < 0.001), with adjustment for age, body mass index, smoking, blood pressure, alcohol use, physical activity, urban residence, and education.

confidence_interval.excerpt: quartile 1) was associated with consumption of the flavonoid quercetin (hazard ratio = 0.6, 95% confidence interval: 0.4, 0.9; P(trend) = 0.015) and Baltic herring (hazard ratio = 2.0, 95% confidence interval: 1.4, 3.0; P(trend) < 0.001), with adjustment for age, body mass index, smoking, blood pressure, alcohol use, physical activity, urban residence, and education.

comparison.excerpt: risk (quartile 4 vs. quartile 1) was associated with consumption of the flavonoid quercetin

design.excerpt: Risk was prospectively assessed in the Alpha-Tocopherol Beta-Carotene Cancer Prevention Study (1985-2002) cohort

timing.excerpt: At enrollment, demographic, health, and dietary history information was recorded.

smoking_status.excerpt: Individuals who smoked less than 5 cigarettes/day, with chronic renal insufficiency or prior cancer, were excluded.

studies.disease_hierarchy_reference_basis: Selected parent reference risk is an analysis proxy for inherited subtype estimates; it is not a published subtype risk.
studies.disease_hierarchy_pooling_reason: Selected eligible estimate for this study/population; parent-direct preference, then adjusted/primary estimate.

disease_hierarchy_method: Eligible child evidence belongs to the selected general category. Parent-direct estimates are preferred within each overlapping study/population; otherwise one adjusted/primary child estimate is selected. Disjoint populations require explicit documentation.
